HIPAA-H-1-RiskAnalysis.evidence: risk assessment of its primary patient-records database in 2024
HIPAA-H-1-RiskAnalysis.reason: The document describes a one-time assessment of a single system rather than a periodic, comprehensive risk analysis covering all ePHI systems.

HIPAA-H-2-SanctionPolicy.reason: The policy contains no documented sanction or disciplinary policy for workforce members who violate security policies.

HIPAA-H-3-WorkforceAccess.evidence: All Acme engineers receive access to the production environment on their first day.
HIPAA-H-3-WorkforceAccess.reason: The policy describes granting access but provides no role-based control or documented procedure for terminating/deprovisioning access.

HIPAA-H-4-SecurityTraining.evidence: New hires complete a 45-minute HIPAA security orientation during onboarding week
HIPAA-H-4-SecurityTraining.reason: The policy describes only a one-time onboarding training and does not specify recurring security awareness training for the workforce.

HIPAA-H-5-ContingencyPlan.evidence: Production databases are backed up nightly to a second cloud region.
HIPAA-H-5-ContingencyPlan.reason: The document addresses backups but does not mention disaster recovery or emergency-mode operations as required by the rule.

HIPAA-H-6-AccessControl.reason: The policy explicitly allows shared accounts, which violates the requirement for unique user identifiers on ePHI systems.

HIPAA-H-7-AuditControls.reason: The policy describes security controls but contains no mention of audit logging for ePHI systems or any periodic log review.

HIPAA-H-8-TransmissionSecurity.reason: The document specifies encryption in transit but provides no indication that ePHI is encrypted at rest.
